title: Four-Step Chicken Piccata
shortDescription: Lemon-caper pan sauce in four straightforward steps
subtitle: Lemon-caper pan sauce in four straightforward steps
description: Lemon-caper pan sauce in four straightforward steps

ingredients.name: Boneless, Skinless Chicken Breasts
ingredients.notes: split into 12 cutlets, pounded ¼ inch

steps.title: Pound and season cutlets
steps.instruction: Working one breast at a time, slice horizontally into three even pieces and pound to ¼ inch between plastic wrap. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Spread flour in a sheet pan and dredge cutlets, shaking off excess — a thin dusting is enough.

steps.title: Sear cutlets in batches
steps.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Sear cutlets in batches without crowding, 2–3 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a warm platter and tent with foil while you finish the sauce.

steps.title: Build the lemon-caper sauce
steps.instruction: Reduce heat to medium. Add garlic and capers to the pan; cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in broth, wine, and lemon zest strips. Simmer, scraping browned bits, until reduced to about ½ cup and slightly syrupy, 8–10 minutes. Off heat, whisk in remaining butter and lemon juice until glossy.

steps.title: Coat cutlets in lemon-caper sauce
steps.instruction: Return cutlets and any resting juices to the skillet. Turn each piece once in the sauce over low heat until warmed through, about 1 minute — do not boil or the cutlets toughen. Spoon glossy sauce over every portion and scatter parsley at the line. Plate two to three cutlets per firefighter with pasta or crusty bread; hold sauced chicken covered at 200°F up to 15 minutes if a call delays seating.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Four-Step Chicken Piccata with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Four-Step Chicken Piccata on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Lemon-caper pan sauce in four straightforward steps. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
